For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:
https://images.redhat.com/
mitigations: Disable Web-STOMP and Web-MQTT where unnecessary, or avoid those non-default authentication options until an updated build is deployed.
Disable the JMS topic exchange plugin if unused and restrict binding permissions to trusted users.

Disable the shovel management extension on brokers that do not need to manage shovels over HTTP. Enable rabbitmq_shovel explicitly first so it stays active if it was only pulled in as a dependency:

 rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_shovel
 rabbitmq-plugins disable rabbitmq_shovel_management

This removes the /api/shovels endpoint. Accounts with the policymaker or administrator tag can still delete shovels through /api/parameters, which enforces the correct role check. If the endpoint has to stay available, remove the monitoring tag from any account that should not be able to stop message flow.
Disable the stream plugin if unused, and restrict stream access to trusted clients.
Replace wildcard CORS with explicit trusted origins and avoid administrator Basic credentials in browsers used for untrusted sites.
Restrict AMQP access to trusted clients until an updated build is deployed.
Restrict Management API access and monitoring-tag accounts, or disable the Management plugin where it is not needed.
Restrict management-tagged accounts and disable stream management where it is not needed.
Restrict monitoring access and disable federation management where it is not needed.
Restrict publish access to trusted clients; broker memory alarms offer only partial protection until an updated build is deployed.
Restrict that access or disable stream management where it is not needed.
Restrict untrusted network access to AMQP listeners; disable AMQP 1.0 support if unused.
To mitigate this issue, restrict access to the RabbitMQ management UI to trusted administrators only. Ensure that administrative interfaces are not exposed to untrusted networks.
